opportunities.title: Initial RFQ qualification brief
opportunities.hypothesis: A structured first-pass brief may reduce repeated reading before engineering review.
opportunities.whyItMayBeWrong: The current process may already be structured, low-volume, or constrained by engineering capacity rather than request preparation.
missingEvidence: Median time to first technical response
aiPrepares: Extracts part, material, dimensions, tolerance, volume and timing
Creates a review brief and clarification questions
opportunities.humanDecides: An engineer approves the interpretation, selection and every technical commitment.
opportunities.practicalResult: A consistent engineering-ready brief instead of repeated first-pass reading.
opportunities.metric: Median time to first technically substantive response, paired with input completeness.
opportunities.stopRule: Stop if cycle time does not improve or engineer corrections exceed the agreed threshold.

Run expert review and measure corrections

site.title: A testable RFQ preparation hypothesis for NordForm Machines

outreach.subject: NordForm Machines: one testable RFQ workflow hypothesis
outreach.body:
Hello Commercial Director,

The fictional NordForm material combines configurable machinery with engineering support. That does not prove an internal problem, but it suggests one testable question: could a structured first-pass RFQ brief reduce repeated reading before engineering review?

I prepared a short, sourced work sample that shows the hypothesis, its limits, human decision points, and a 30-day validation design without invented ROI. I am exploring AI commercial-operations roles where I can own this kind of work.

Would 15 minutes be useful to confirm or disprove three assumptions?

Egor Example
outreach.optOut: If this is not relevant, let me know and I will not follow up.
